topics.title: Revision of jss two work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recall food classes and clothing construction basics.
The students should be able to identify different types of nutrients and their sources.
Introduction:
We have learned about food nutrients and clothing construction in JSS two. Today we will revise these important topics to prepare for new work.
Content:
Food classes include carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, minerals and fats. Carbohydrates give us energy like pounded yam and rice. Proteins help growth like beans and fish. Vitamins keep us healthy like oranges and vegetables. Minerals build strong bones like milk and leafy greens.
Clothing construction involves cutting fabric and sewing pieces together. We use patterns to guide cutting. Different fabrics need different needles and threads. A well-made garment has strong seams and fits well.
Class activity:
Students will complete a quick quiz matching food items to their nutrient classes and identify different sewing tools.
Evaluation questions:
1. Name three food rich in carbohydrates.
2. What is the purpose of vitamins in our diet?
3. List two tools used in clothing construction.
4. Why is it important to choose the right needle for fabric?
Summary:
Today we revised food nutrients and clothing construction basics which are essential for our home economics studies.

topics.title: Family living
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify family needs and resources.
The students should be able to create a simple family budget.
Introduction:
Every family has basic needs and resources to manage. Today we will learn how families plan their resources to meet these needs.
Content:
Family needs include food, shelter, clothing, education and healthcare. Resources are money, time, skills and materials. A good family budget helps allocate resources wisely. For example, a family might spend 40% on food, 20% on rent, 15% on education and 10% on transport with some savings.
Family income comes from salaries, farming, trading or other work. Expenses must be less than or equal to income. Saving money for future needs is important, like during harmattan season when prices of goods increase.
Class activity:
Students will create a simple budget for a family of four with a monthly income of 50,000 naira.
Evaluation questions:
1. List three basic family needs.
2. What is a family budget?
3. Why is saving important in family finance?
4. How might a family adjust their budget during economic hardship?
Summary:
Good family living requires proper planning of needs and resources to ensure a comfortable life.

topics.title: Consumer education
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain wise buying skills.
The students should be able to compare different products before purchasing.
Introduction:
As consumers, we make buying decisions every day at the market or supermarket. Today we will learn how to make smart choices when spending money.
Content:
Wise buying means getting value for money. Before buying, consider needs versus wants. Compare prices, quality, quantity and expiry dates. For example, when buying rice, check if it's locally grown imported rice, the price per kilogram, and how long it can be stored.
Advertisements can influence our decisions. We should be careful not to be tricked by fancy packaging. Reading labels helps us understand what we are buying. A good consumer asks questions and checks facts before spending money.
Class activity:
Students will compare two brands of the same product (like powdered milk or detergent) and decide which offers better value.
Evaluation questions:
1. What does wise buying mean?
2. List three things to consider before making a purchase.
3. How can advertisements affect our buying decisions?
4. Why is it important to check product labels?
Summary:
Being a smart consumer helps us save money and get the best value for our purchases.

topics.title: Food nutrients
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to state the classes of food nutrients.
The students should be able to list sources of different nutrients.
The students should be able to plan a balanced meal.
Introduction:
We eat food to get nutrients that keep our bodies healthy. Today we will learn about different nutrients and how to plan meals with them.
Content:
Food nutrients are carbohydrates, proteins, fats and oils, vitamins, minerals and water. Carbohydrates give energy from foods like rice, yam, and garri. Proteins build muscles from beans, fish, and meat. Fats provide energy from groundnut oil and palm oil. Vitamins and minerals come from fruits, vegetables, and milk.
A balanced meal contains all nutrient classes. For example, a meal could include rice (carbohydrate), beans (protein), fish (protein), vegetable stew (vitamins), and palm oil (fat). Water is also essential for all body functions.
Class activity:
Students will plan a balanced meal for a family of four using local Nigerian foods.
Evaluation questions:
1. Name the six classes of food nutrients.
2. Give two examples of protein-rich foods in Nigeria.
3. Why are vitamins important for our health?
4. How would you plan a balanced meal with 500 naira?
Summary:
Understanding food nutrients helps us plan healthy meals that keep our bodies strong and functioning well.

topics.title: Meal planning and service
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to plan a meal.
The students should be able to cook and serve a simple dish.
Introduction:
After learning about food nutrients, we now need to know how to plan, cook and serve meals properly. This is an important life skill.
Content:
Meal planning involves choosing foods that are nutritious, affordable and liked by the family. Consider the time available for cooking and the equipment needed. For example, a simple meal plan might include jollof rice for lunch and yam porridge for dinner.
Cooking requires following steps carefully. Wash hands before cooking. Use clean utensils. Cook food thoroughly to kill germs. Serving food attractively makes it more appealing. Food should be served at the right temperature and in clean dishes.
Class activity:
Students will work in groups to cook a simple Nigerian dish like fried rice or moi-moi.
Evaluation questions:
1. What factors should be considered when planning a meal?
2. Why is it important to wash hands before cooking?
3. List three steps in proper food service.
4. How does cooking food thoroughly help prevent illness?
Summary:
Proper meal planning and service ensures that food is both nutritious and enjoyable for the family.

topics.title: Food preservation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain different methods of food preservation.
The students should be able to preserve a simple food item.
Introduction:
Food can spoil quickly in our hot climate. Today we will learn methods to preserve food so it lasts longer and doesn't waste.
Content:
Food preservation keeps food from spoiling. Common methods include drying, salting, sugaring, smoking, and refrigeration. Drying removes moisture like when we make dried fish or pepper. Salting draws out water like in smoked fish. Sugaring is used for fruits like mangoes. Smoking adds flavor and preserves meat like bushmeat.
In Nigerian homes, we often sun-dry tomatoes, pepper, and fish to preserve them. During the harmattan season, we can dry foods faster. Properly preserved food can be stored for months and used when fresh foods are not available.
Class activity:
Students will preserve mangoes by drying them in the sun or salting them.
Evaluation questions:
1. Why do we preserve food?
2. Name three methods of food preservation used in Nigeria.
3. How does drying help preserve food?
4. What care should be taken when preserving food at home?
Summary:
Food preservation helps reduce waste and ensures we have food available all year round.

topics.title: Clothing construction
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain pattern drafting basics.
The students should be able to draft a simple block pattern.
Introduction:
Making clothes requires proper planning and cutting of fabric. Today we will learn the basics of pattern drafting which is the foundation of clothing construction.
Content:
Pattern drafting is creating templates for cutting fabric. Basic patterns include bodice, skirt, and sleeve blocks. These are made by taking body measurements like chest, waist, hips, and length. Measurements must be accurate for a good fit.
To draft a simple bodice block, we start with a rectangle based on chest and length measurements. We mark darts for shaping at the bust and waist. The pattern is then cut and used to cut fabric. Different fabrics require different seam allowances, usually 1-1.5cm.
Class activity:
Students will take measurements and draft a simple bodice block pattern on paper.
Evaluation questions:
1. What is pattern drafting?
2. Name three basic body measurements needed for pattern drafting.
3. Why are darts important in clothing construction?
4. What is a seam allowance and why is it needed?
Summary:
Pattern drafting is an essential skill that allows us to create well-fitting clothes from scratch.

topics.title: Sewing machine mastery
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate proper sewing machine maintenance.
The students should be able to sew a simple item using a sewing machine.
Introduction:
The sewing machine is an important tool for making clothes efficiently. Today we will learn how to care for it and use it to stitch fabrics together.
Content:
A sewing machine needs regular maintenance to work well. Before using it, oil moving parts like the shuttle race and needle bar. Clean lint from the bobbin area after each use. Thread the machine correctly by following the thread path from spool to needle. Different fabrics need different stitch lengths and tensions.
Basic sewing includes straight stitching, backstitching, and zigzag stitching. Straight stitching is used for seams. Backstitching secures the beginning and end of seams. Zigzag stitching prevents fabric from fraying. Always start and end with backstitches to keep stitches from coming apart.
Class activity:
Students will sew a simple pillowcase using straight stitching and proper seam allowances.
Evaluation questions:
1. Name two parts of a sewing machine that need regular oiling.
2. Why is it important to clean a sewing machine regularly?
3. What is the purpose of backstitching?
4. How does stitch length affect the quality of a seam?
Summary:
Proper care and use of the sewing machine helps create well-made and durable clothing items.

topics.title: Home care
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain cleaning routines for different parts of the home.
The students should be able to create a home cleaning schedule.
Introduction:
A clean home is healthy and comfortable. Today we will learn proper cleaning routines and how to organize them effectively.
Content:
Home care involves regular cleaning of different areas. The kitchen needs daily cleaning to prevent germs and pests. Sweep and mop floors, wipe counters, and clean the sink. The bathroom should be cleaned weekly with disinfectant to kill germs. Bedrooms need making beds, dusting furniture, and sweeping floors.
A cleaning schedule helps organize work. For example, Monday could be kitchen day, Tuesday bathroom day, Wednesday living room day, and so on. Different seasons require special attention - during harmattan, more dusting is needed; during rainy season, floors may need more frequent cleaning.
Class activity:
Students will create a weekly cleaning schedule for a typical Nigerian home.
Evaluation questions:
1. Why is regular home cleaning important?
2. Name two areas that need daily cleaning in a home.
3. How might cleaning needs change during different seasons in Nigeria?
4. What cleaning supplies are essential for a Nigerian home?
Summary:
Proper home care routines keep our living spaces healthy and comfortable for the whole family.

topics.title: Revision and BECE practice
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to answer past BECE questions on home economics.
The students should be able to identify common mistakes in home economics answers.
Introduction:
As we approach the BECE exams, it's important to practice with past questions to understand the exam format and requirements.
Content:
Past BECE questions cover all topics we've studied this term. Questions may ask about food nutrients, meal planning, food preservation, clothing construction, sewing, and home care. Answers should be clear, concise and directly address the question. For example, a question might ask 'Explain three methods of food preservation' and require specific examples like drying, salting, and smoking.
Common mistakes include not reading questions carefully, not providing enough examples, and not organizing answers logically. Time management is also important - practice answering questions within the time limit. Reviewing marked papers helps understand where improvements are needed.
Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to answer and mark past BECE home economics questions.
Evaluation questions:
1. What topics are commonly tested in BECE home economics?
2. How should you structure an answer to an exam question?
3. Name two common mistakes to avoid in exam answers.
4. Why is time management important during exams?
Summary:
Practicing with past questions helps prepare for the BECE by familiarizing us with the exam format and improving our answering skills.
